text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000114 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation, including on low-complexity patients, but only three documented 99215 claims exist, so the records cannot confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 billing is not explained by panel acuity alone. The elevated share shows up at every complexity level with one or more conditions, and the low-complexity sample includes 99215s on single-condition or no-condition patients (e.g., C0061966, C0062047, C0062102, C0062193). The high-complexity sample does show genuinely multimorbid patients where 99215 is plausible (e.g., C0062100, C0062150). The documentation is too thin to judge: one of three documented 99215s (C0062000) was below the billed level, and one low-complexity 99215 (C0061966) was documented at high MDM, so neither direction is established. The 99213/99214 records were fully supported, and only 1 of 22 data-reviewed notes lacked a lab line, which gives little sign of inflated notes. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with C0062193, C0062047 and C0062102, to test whether those visits truly reflect high-complexity decision-making."}
